what: Authored terminal-status records for census rows, read by scripts/build-registries.mjs. Master prompt section 13.1 requires the actionable-item census to close both ways, and names exactly two escape hatches for a row no rendered control demonstrates: an explicit decision-blocked record, or an explicit not-applicable record. Until audit round 4 finding R4-B05 the generator could emit NEITHER string, so 4,704 rows sat in not-represented, which is neither of the two permitted terminal states, and the escape hatch the section names was unreachable by construction. This file is that hatch.
whyAuthoredRatherThanDerived: A terminal status is a judgement about the source, not a fact the route tree can compute. Derivation is what produces the other three statuses (demonstrated-in-storyboard, mounted-in-another-screen, not-represented) and it is deliberately left alone. What is added here is a record a human wrote, with the four things master prompt section 9.2 requires before a Not applicable classification may stand at all: a reason, an owner, source or decision evidence, and the rows it applies to named one by one.
whatThisFileMayNeverBecome: The number this hatch exists beside is 4,704 rows in not-represented, and the way to make that number small is to relabel it. That is expressly forbidden: an override is legitimate only where the frozen source itself says the row is not a thing a rendered control can demonstrate, or where a named open decision blocks it. After this file, the honest position is still a large not-represented count, and the coverage dashboard publishes it beside the overrides rather than instead of them. tests/coverage/census-closure.test.ts holds both halves.
evidenceLineMeaning: A one-based line number in the frozen source ../AVIIXA_Production_Product_Blueprint.md, sha256 47bd18db467817f3edbe3329c8ae5e332013871aaa2df08c2be6fc5afa8d0b27. Recorded as a bare number with a verbatim quotation beside it so a reader checks the line rather than the record.
whyTheWholeLineIsTranscribed: Audit round 5 finding R5-A06. The gate asserted that evidenceQuote is a substring of the cited line, and it could not see that the SAME LINE'S FIRST SENTENCE describes a rendering that refutes the classification the quotation was chosen to support: line 98508 opens 'In the Super Admin extension screen of section 45A.2, every row in this register renders as a locked entry that cannot be given a schedule.' A twenty-word excerpt of a three-sentence line can support almost anything, so every override now transcribes the WHOLE line into evidenceLineVerbatim, which tests/coverage/census-closure.test.ts compares byte-for-byte against the frozen source, and answers the remainder in whatElseThisLineSays. An author may still make the wrong call; they can no longer make it without the contradicting sentence being in the record and in the diff.

overrides.reason: A do-not-use-cron row is a scheduling prohibition, not an actionable UI control. The register names a platform functionality and states why a scheduled sweeper is the wrong mechanism for it; the thing the row describes is what the platform refuses to automate, so the §13.1 census — whose subject is CONTROLS generated from the ControlDefinition registry — has no control to count for it. R5-A06 CORRECTED THE OVERSTATEMENT IN THIS REASON: it used to say that asking whether a rendered control demonstrates one is 'a category error, and answering not-represented implies a screen this build owes and does not owe'. The second half is false, and the evidence line says so itself — the source describes a Super Admin extension screen (section 45A.2) listing all 22 as locked entries that refuse a schedule. That screen IS owed and this build does not ship it. It is recorded here as an owed screen rather than silently classified away, and the distinction that keeps the not-applicable status honest is narrow and stated: a locked entry that refuses a schedule is the ABSENCE of a control, so building §45A.2 would not turn any of these 22 rows into a demonstrated control either. The registry's own countedThing has said as much since the register was first split out: scheduling policy, never an actionable control, and never merged into the 608.
overrides.owner: JBS build controller, under client approval APP-012 (standing autonomous authority to census closure across all fourteen inventories; where a choice is open, pick what is best for the business and proceed).
overrides.evidenceQuote: On tenant surfaces nothing from this register is visible, because the register describes what the platform refuses to do rather than something a tenant configures.
overrides.evidenceLineVerbatim: **Storyboard.** In the Super Admin extension screen of section 45A.2, every row in this register renders as a locked entry that cannot be given a schedule. Attempting to attach a Schedule Definition to a do-not-use-cron control fails with the reason shown, in the same manner the Tenant-Configuration Registry rejects an out-of-bound value rather than accepting and logging it [SoW Fact — §8.19]. On tenant surfaces nothing from this register is visible, because the register describes what the platform refuses to do rather than something a tenant configures.
overrides.whatElseThisLineSays: The line's first two sentences describe a screen this build does not ship: a Super Admin extension screen at section 45A.2 that lists every row of this register as a locked entry, and that refuses an attempt to attach a Schedule Definition with the reason shown. No page in out/ names a DNC- identifier. That is an OWED SCREEN and it is recorded as one here rather than left to be discovered by a reader who opens the cited line. It does not change the status: what §45A.2 renders is a refusal rather than a control, so the row would still have no rendered control to count once the screen exists. If that reading is ever judged wrong, the honest correction is to move all 22 rows to not-represented, not to reword this record.

decisionBlockedOccupancy.whyZeroRatherThanUnwritten: The status is emittable by exactly the same mechanism as not-applicable above, and no census row qualifies for it today. Measured rather than assumed: the build's decision canon at src/disclosure/decisions.ts carries every open source decision this build met, and each one renders its readings with an adopted, client-delegated position under APP-012 rather than blocking a row. The one item genuinely held rather than adopted is DEC-REPORT-001, which blocks two of MOD-DOH-18's five standard report data sets, and those two are ordinals inside a module rather than identifier-keyed census rows, so no row of the fourteen inventories carries them. Writing an override for a row that is not blocked would be the same defect in the other direction. The coverage dashboard states this occupancy on screen rather than leaving a legend entry that nothing can reach.
